$comment: Resolved content baselines for the federated entries in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json.
Deliberately NOT stored in marketplace.json: that file is consumed by Claude Code
against its own marketplace schema, and must not carry keys the plugin loader does
not expect. This sidecar is read only by scripts/check-federated-content.mjs.
Why it exists: a federated entry pins a tag by NAME, and a tag name is mutable.
Re-pointing it at different content is silent - every consumer follows, and the
existing pin check still passes because it only asks whether the tag resolves and
declares the matching version. lore-cli and quest-cli both had v0.6.0 deleted and
recreated on 2026-09-10/11 (OMARK-43); the skill content happened to be unchanged,
but nothing in CI could have told us if it had not been.
To update: re-resolve the chain yourself (tag ref -> tag object -> commit -> root
tree -> skills subtree), confirm the content is what you intend to ship, and record
the new SHA here in the same change that moves the pin. Updating this file is the
act of saying 'I verified this content', so do not update it to make CI go green.
Release handshake, agreed with the lore-cli session and tracked there as LCLI-469:
lore-cli messages this repository at tag-cut time with the tag name, the tag object
SHA, the commit it peels to, and the resolved skills/ tree SHA, so a new release
arrives with its baseline rather than as a red check here. The same is expected of
quest-cli. Do not take those SHAs on trust - they are a head start, not a
verification; re-resolve them here before recording, which is the whole point of
this file. If a pin bump ever lands without its baseline moving, the checker fails
on purpose rather than silently checking the wrong tag.

opum-lore.note: OMARK-66. Real content change, not bookkeeping: skills/lore/SKILL.md was rewritten (LCLI-573, opum-ai/lore-cli#237). Chain re-resolved independently via the GitHub API rather than taken from lore-cli's LCLI-469 handshake message -- tag ref v0.9.2 -> tag object ed4153bee35db7c0ee3b910a97d79d9f0ce7f12e (type=tag), also cross-checked via `git ls-remote --tags` as a second independent source -> peels to commit 71f2c1e470aac36465871652ddf5347d5b0382c0 -> root tree 338c9c93afd340c70f8d0d929c4ee161dfbb27f0 -> skills subtree ce580cd17d1da6a61ddb53f649398719b9262f96. .claude-plugin/plugin.json at the tag self-declares version 0.9.2, confirmed by direct GitHub API read. npm dist-tags.latest confirmed independently as 0.9.2 on the main package and all 6 platform packages. Compare API diff (v0.9.1...v0.9.2) shows exactly one path under skills/ changed: skills/lore/SKILL.md (modified) -- confirmed by fetching and diffing both blobs directly, not by trusting the relay's description: retrieval-first guidance added (`lore query` then `lore read` before `lore context`), `--max-tokens` restated as a hard ceiling (was advisory), the Backlog commit-side-effect preflight language dropped in favor of a backend-scoped note (link/unlink/rename/sync commit tracker files on the Backlog backend only), and the file now carries a generated-file footer. Ran `lore check` under 0.9.2 (via `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.9.2`, not the older globally-installed 0.9.0) against this repo's docs/ bundle: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. `lore agents --check` under 0.9.2 reported both this repo's CLAUDE.md managed block and .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md out of date against the new generator output (expected per the release note, since both were last regenerated under 0.9.0); regenerated both in the same change via `lore agents --force`, re-ran `lore agents --check` to confirm exit 0.
